subject: Request: Locked-Down Inference — No Tuning, Response IP, and Cross-Border Transit
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@hearthbridge.com>, Legal Ops <legalops@hearthbridge.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Locked-Down Inference — No Tuning, Response IP, and Cross-Border Transit

Hi Sam / Legal team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Per our discussion, HearthBridge asked for three commitments to be reflected in the DPA / SOW addendum before legal sign-off:

1) No model tuning or use of HearthBridge interaction data for model improvement (no-training)
2) Clear ownership / licensing for prompts and generated responses (we discussed response IP vs. license to use)
3) Controls on cross-border processing and an auditable subprocessor list + evidentiary path

Attached is a short amendment (redline) that tracks the language we suggested (redwood-dpa-amendment-diff.docx) and a proposed SOW clause for inference-only processing (no-tune-sow-addendum.pdf).

Quick implementation notes so your ops team can validate feasibility:
- Customer interactions will be marked as "service-processing" and routed to isolated inference clusters.
- We propose ephemeral KV cache retention of 2 hours by default for session continuity; logs for debugging retained 7 days unless you request longer/shorter.
- When you choose onshore processing, we pin to a region and restrict cross-border fallbacks (we can include a hard-coded region list in the DPA).

Ask: Can you confirm whether HearthBridge needs a contractual clause stating explicit assignment of response IP to the customer (absolute assignment) or whether a perpetual, exclusive license suffices? That will change the phrasing in section 3.2 of the amendment.

Next steps: If you’re comfortable with the redline we’ll route to procurement for signature. Happy to hop on another 30-min call if that helps.

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-dpa-amendment-diff.docx (docx, 28 KB), no-tune-sow-addendum.pdf (pdf, 12 KB)

Subject: Re: Request: Locked-Down Inference — No Tuning, Response IP, and Cross-Border Transit

Priya — thanks for the summary and the docs. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side:

- On "response IP": HB legal prefers assignment where generated responses are owned by HearthBridge. Can you confirm Redwood is comfortable with an assignment (not just license) for outputs derived from customer inputs? If assignment is a no-go, we need to discuss a strong, exclusive license instead.
- On retention: is there an option to set the KV cache to "session-only" (no persisted KV at all) for particularly sensitive workflows?
- Subprocessors: can you share the list (or categories) up-front, and confirm you will notify us before adding any new subprocessor?

Procurement timeline: we hope to get to countersign by the end of November. If Redwood can confirm the three items above (assignment vs license; session-only option; subprocessors + notification), Procurement will push the amendment through.

Sam Ortega
Senior Counsel, HearthBridge Health
legalops@hearthbridge.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortega <sam.ortega@hearthbridge.com>, Legal Ops <legalops@hearthbridge.com>
Cc: Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Locked-Down Inference — No Tuning, Response IP, and Cross-Border Transit

Sam — thanks, answers below and a proposed compromise we use with similar regulated customers: 

- Assignment vs License: Redwood cannot wholesale assign model weights or underlying model IP. For generated responses we can offer a: 
  a) customer ownership of responses (assignment) for outputs stored/ingested by the customer (explicit assignment clause), and
  b) a perpetual, exclusive license for any outputs that remain in our ephemeral systems for less than the configured retention window. 

  Practically, we recommend the following contract language (we'll redline it into the doc): "Customer shall own all outputs and responses exported or stored by Customer. Redwood grants Customer an exclusive, perpetual, transferable license to outputs generated by the Service for the duration necessary to access service features; Redwood shall not use Customer outputs for model improvement."

- Session-only KV: yes — we can enable a session-only mode (no persisted KV or prefix caching) as an opt-in toggle per project. We’ll call this out in the SOW and provide an operation flag for your engineers.

- Subprocessors & Notification: we provide an up-to-date subprocessor inventory (categories + company names) on our compliance page and will add contract language requiring 30-day notice before adding processors with data-access capability. For highly restricted accounts we can gate new subprocessors behind an approval workflow.

Operational evidence we can provide for procurement/legal review:
- SOC 2 report and scope statement (we'll provide the latest PDF)
- Subprocessor attestation pack (signed statements)
- Demo of session-only mode + log retention configuration (recorded video)
- Exportable access logs for the inference cluster for a 30-day lookback

Connor (cc'd) — can you confirm the UI flag name for session-only mode and whether enabling it disables both KV and ephemeral log storage? Also confirm default retention values we mentioned to HearthBridge (KV = 2h, logs = 7d).

Best,
Priya

Forwarding operational confirmation and suggested clause text.

Operational confirmations:
- Session-only mode: UI flag name = "inference.session_persistence" (boolean). When true, KV prefix caching is disabled and no KV data is persisted beyond in-memory process lifecycle; debug traces are still recorded to ephemeral logs unless the "ephemeral.debug_logs" flag is set to false.
- Defaults: inference.session_persistence = false (default), KV retention = 2h, inference.logs.retention = 7d. We can set defaults per account at provisioning time.
- Onshore processing: we can pin processing to US regions and prevent cross-border fallback unless you explicitly request it. This is a provisioning option and will be reflected in the account config and the DPA.
- Subprocessors: current list (summary): compute providers (Redwood Dedicated partners), cloud storage for logs (vendor A), monitoring/observability (vendor B). Full inventory + attestation pack attached once PRD is approved.

Suggested contract text (snippet for your counsel):
"Redwood will not use Customer content, prompts, or generated responses to train, fine-tune, or improve any models, nor will Redwood permit its subprocessors to do so. Customer shall own outputs and responses stored or exported by Customer. Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, exclusive license to outputs retained only transiently by Redwood for the minimum duration necessary to provide the service. Redwood shall provide a subprocessors inventory and 30 days' notice before adding subprocessors with data-access capability."

Attachments referenced above: redwood-dpa-amendment-diff.docx (tracked changes), no-tune-sow-addendum.pdf (SOW language).

Next steps: Priya — happy to incorporate counsel feedback and produce a clean amendment for countersign. Sam — if you confirm you can accept the assignment+license compromise above Procurement will move forward on your timeline.

– Priyom Das
Principal Product Ops Engineer, Redwood Inference
